sources.title: Grok 4 Fast launch, September 19, 2025
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27 full launch read. Both Fast modes use the same weights, selected by system prompts. The opening says Fast is built on learnings from Grok 4 and describes smaller/faster models; this is not an explicit unchanged-base relationship to Grok 4. Benchmark, token-efficiency and price comparisons supply no nominal total or activated count. The exact reasoning/non-reasoning slugs are generally available September 19, 2025 with 2M context.

sources.title: Grok 4 Fast model card
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27 review of the complete seven-page original PDF. Section 1 says Grok 4 Fast was pretrained on a general-purpose corpus and post-trained on tasks and tool use; Section 3.1 details its data recipe, reinforcement learning and supervised fine-tuning. Tables 1-3 are safety/behavior evaluations. No nominal total, active count, named unchanged base or neural topology is disclosed.

sources.title: xAI Grok 4 Fast archived provider specifications
sources.evidence: Explicitly distinguishes xai.grok-4-fast-reasoning, which generates thinking tokens, from the non-reasoning mode. Specifies 2,000,000 combined context, text/image input, text output and API function calling. Provider page now records retirement; historical specifications remain visible.

sources.title: May 15, 2026 model retirement
sources.evidence: Exact grok-4-fast-reasoning slug retired May 15, 2026 at noon Pacific and redirects to Grok 4.3 with low reasoning effort. The replacement has different context and pricing; these are not treated as original Fast specifications.

sources.title: Original reasoning-model documentation route
sources.evidence: The exact historical model route redirects to the current general model roster. It no longer supplies the original model specification, so current replacement specifications are not inferred from this redirect.

sources.title: Enterprise terms covering the xAI API, June 27, 2025
sources.evidence: Read the complete web-extracted terms; direct HTTP returned 403. Sections 1, 2 and 4 grant limited service access, reserve underlying technology rights and restrict reverse engineering and derivative copying. Supports descriptive proprietary hosted licensing.

sources.title: xAI public checkpoint inventory
sources.evidence: Fresh organization inventory returns Grok 1 and Grok 2 repositories, with no Grok 4 Fast checkpoint. Considered alongside explicit hosted distribution, not alone as proof of license.

sources.title: Later Grok 4.1 Fast announcement
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27 full successor announcement read, including benchmark comparisons with Grok 4 Fast. Reports tool-calling and factuality performance, not total/active parameters of original Fast; no named size-preserving lineage supplies a count.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 review found no published nominal total in the original launch/card, later xAI reports or original research comparisons. Shared weights connect only the two Fast response modes. Built on learnings from Grok 4 does not identify an unchanged Grok 4 base; no size can be inherited from that wording. The later Grok 4.3 redirect is a replacement, not original-model lineage.

active_parameters_b.note: Fresh separate active-count search found no developer disclosure or original benchmark convention for this exact mode. Later comparison tables give performance or dollar cost for Grok 4 Fast, not an activated count. Shared response-mode weights and 40% fewer thinking tokens do not measure parameters activated per token; no total-to-active equality is inferred.

architecture.note: Unified architecture describes the shared reasoning/non-reasoning weights and prompting. It does not disclose Transformer, dense or MoE structure. No network subtype is inferred from other Grok models or rumors.

context_window.note: Original Fast context is explicitly two million combined tokens. The later Grok 4.3 redirect has a different limit and does not revise this historical model record.

modalities.note: Exact historical provider documentation identifies text/image input and text output. Clear unsupported audio/video input assertions; browsing video content through a tool does not establish the original API input contract.

reasoning.note: This exact mode generates thinking tokens before its response. The non-reasoning sibling uses the same weights with a different system prompt.

tool_call.note: Documented native tool-use training and exact API function-calling support.

Enterprise terms covering the xAI API, June 27, 2025

patch.notes: Released September 19, 2025. Reasoning and non-reasoning modes share weights and differ through system prompting. Total and active parameter counts and neural network architecture remain undisclosed; xAI does not identify Fast as an unchanged Grok 4 base. Historical specifications are text/image input, text output and 2,000,000 context tokens. Since May 15, 2026, the original reasoning slug redirects to Grok 4.3 with low reasoning effort; this replacement does not revise original Fast specifications.

summary: Retained the original name, release-date and modality corrections. The October 27 parameter re-audit separately rechecked total and active sizes in the launch, complete technical card, later xAI disclosures and original research comparisons. Neither count is established, and both now have explicit null patches. Same-weight reasoning/non-reasoning modes are documented, but Grok 4 ancestry is not an unchanged-base statement; the Grok 4.3 redirect remains a later replacement. All other twelve field assessments are preserved.

parameter_reaudit.outcome: Retain parameters_b=null and active_parameters_b=null, both undisclosed, after fresh separate review.
parameter_reaudit.lineage_assessment: The original launch explicitly shares Fast weights between reasoning and non-reasoning modes. It says built on learnings from Grok 4, describes smaller/faster models and separately compares Fast to Grok 4; it does not name an unchanged Grok 4 base, fine-tune or size-preserving variant. The original card describes Fast pretraining and post-training without a numerical architecture. This supports mode identity but supplies no known-size ancestor. May 15 routing to Grok 4.3 is explicitly a replacement.
parameter_reaudit.later_comparison_assessment: ClinSQL Appendix E names the exact reasoning API ID; its tables have scores/configuration, not counts. ACL 2026 Table 2 explicitly says the seven closed models have undisclosed sizes and reports costs for them; Grok 4 Fast $0.26 is not an active size. ServiceNow Apriel Figure 3 has no Grok point; its Grok comparison rows and larger-model language do not give a count. The partially indexed RSC OPENXRD table also marks Fast U, but full-source access was blocked and it was not adopted as a specification.
parameter_reaudit.search_findings: Fresh bounded total, active/activated, later-comparison and lineage searches found no numerical developer specification or usable original active-count convention. Secondary directories return undisclosed sizes or unsupported Grok 4/MoE/distillation descriptions, which were traced back to the original launch/card and not adopted. No requirement for an exact tensor census was imposed.
